title: Wolfia vs ComplyJet for security questionnaires
summary: ComplyJet is compliance automation with questionnaire and trust center features. Wolfia answers questionnaires and runs a trust center. How they compare.
body_markdown:
ComplyJet is compliance automation with questionnaire and trust center features. Wolfia answers questionnaires and runs a trust center. How they compare.


ComplyJet is a compliance automation platform for SaaS startups, with questionnaire automation and a trust center among its features. Wolfia is an AI agent for security questionnaires, contract review and the trust center, and this page compares the two using only what each company publishes.


## What ComplyJet is


ComplyJet’s homepage says, “We own compliance, so you can keep building.” It is built for SaaS startups, automates evidence collection, recommends an auditor and guides teams through the audit, for frameworks that include SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR and PCI DSS. ComplyJet says questionnaire automation is included in its plans rather than sold as a separate module, with answers pre-populated from a company’s policies, controls, certifications and prior questionnaire history. Its trust center is a security page that shares certifications and compliance status, with NDA acceptance required before sensitive documents download.


## What Wolfia is


Wolfia is an AI agent for security questionnaires, contract review and the trust center. It answers security questionnaires, DDQs and RFPs from a company’s own documents and past answers, gives every answer a cited source, and leaves an answer empty when no document supports it. It works on Excel, Word and PDF files and exports them in their original format, and a Chrome extension fills answers back into web portals. The[Wolfia facts page](https://wolfia.com/facts) lists the rest, including hosting on Amazon Web Services in the United States and SOC 2 Type II.


## ComplyJet and Wolfia side by side


ComplyJet cells come from ComplyJet’s own pages, read 26 November 2026, and Wolfia cells from Wolfia’s published facts.


ComplyJet Wolfia


Primary use Compliance automation for SaaS startups, with questionnaire automation and a trust center in the same platform An AI agent for security questionnaires, contract review and the trust center


Security questionnaires Drafts the full response from your controls and evidence and flags anything that needs a manual answer; names SIG Lite, CAIQ, NIST-based, VSAQ and custom questionnaires Answers security questionnaires and DDQs from your own documents and past answers ([Questionnaire Agent](https://wolfia.com/products/questionnaire-automation) )


File formats Imports Excel, Word, PDF, CSV and Google Sheets, and exports back in the original format Excel, Word and PDF, exported back in the original format


Web portals Lists “Online portal support for common platforms” The Chrome extension extracts the questions from web portals and fills the answers back ([Chrome Extension Agent](https://wolfia.com/products/chrome-extension) )


Trust center A security page for certifications and compliance status, with NDA acceptance before sensitive downloads and a signed copy stored, a sub-processor list and document access requests Access requests and online NDA signing, where one signed NDA carries across documents ([Trust Center](https://wolfia.com/products/trust-center) )


RFPs Not stated on ComplyJet’s site Answers RFPs from the same documents and past answers


Contract review Not stated on ComplyJet’s site AI contract review and obligation tracking, with redlines exported as tracked changes ([Customer Contract Intelligence](https://wolfia.com/products/customer-contract-intelligence) )


Knowledge sources Your ComplyJet policies, controls, certifications and evidence, plus prior questionnaire history Including Google Drive, Confluence, SharePoint, OneDrive, GitHub, GitLab, Glean, Guru, Slab, Mintlify and Letter AI ([Knowledge Base Agent](https://wolfia.com/products/knowledge-base-agent) )


Citations Not stated on ComplyJet’s site Every answer comes with a cited source


Human review “Your team approves every answer” and answers are not submitted automatically Your subject matter experts review the drafts and only handle the questions where Wolfia is unsure or found no source ([Questionnaire Agent](https://wolfia.com/products/questionnaire-automation) )


Pricing The pricing page lists Core from $7,999 or $9,999 a year and Plus from $9,999 or $11,999 a year behind a 3-year and 1-year plan toggle; the questionnaire automation and trust center pages list $5,000 a year for one framework and $8,000 for two Plans start at $500 a month ([Pricing](https://wolfia.com/pricing) )


Pricing model Flat price per company for up to 50 employees, by number of frameworks, with no per-seat fees; plans list one external audit included Every plan covers security questionnaires, contract reviews and the trust center, with unlimited users; pricing scales with volume, not headcount


Hosting region Not stated on the ComplyJet pages read; ComplyJet’s trust center at trust.complyjet.com could not be opened on 26 November 2026 Amazon Web Services in the United States ([Wolfia trust center](https://trust.wolfia.com/) )


Certifications Not stated on the ComplyJet pages read; ComplyJet’s trust center at trust.complyjet.com could not be opened on 26 November 2026 SOC 2 Type II, and certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework


Free trial The homepage has a “Start Free Trial” link; trial length not stated on ComplyJet’s site A “Get started for free” sign-up on wolfia.com; paid plans are scoped on one short call ([Pricing](https://wolfia.com/pricing) )


## Where Wolfia is ahead


Each point below is backed by the table above or by the page it links.


- Wolfia answers RFPs and reviews contracts on the same plan as security questionnaires. ComplyJet’s site states neither RFPs nor contract review.
- Every Wolfia answer comes with a cited source, and an answer is left empty when no document supports it. ComplyJet’s site does not state citations.
- Wolfia names every portal it fills on its[portals page](https://wolfia.com/portals) . ComplyJet lists “online portal support for common platforms” without naming them.


## Which team each fits


ComplyJet fits a startup of up to 50 employees that is working toward SOC 2, ISO 27001 or another framework and wants its questionnaire answers and trust center to draw on the same compliance program, for one flat company price whose plan cards list an external audit as included.


Wolfia fits a team that already has its policies and reports and spends its time on inbound security questionnaires, DDQs and RFPs in files and web portals, and that wants a trust center and contract review on the same plan. It also answers security questions in Slack through the[Slack Agent](https://wolfia.com/products/slack-autorespond) , and in Claude and ChatGPT through the[Wolfia connector](https://wolfia.com/blog/connect-wolfia-to-claude-and-chatgpt) .

## FAQ


### Is ComplyJet a security questionnaire tool?


ComplyJet is a compliance automation platform for SaaS startups. It says questionnaire automation is included in its plans, with answers drafted from a company’s policies, controls, certifications and prior questionnaire history, and reviewed by the company’s own team before sending.


### How much does ComplyJet cost?


ComplyJet’s pages show two sets of figures. Its pricing page lists Core from $7,999 or $9,999 a year and Plus from $9,999 or $11,999 a year, behind a 3-year and 1-year plan toggle. Its questionnaire automation and trust center pages list $5,000 a year for one framework and $8,000 a year for two.


### How much does Wolfia cost?


Wolfia plans start at $500 a month. Every plan covers security questionnaires, contract reviews and the trust center, and includes unlimited users.


### Which file formats do ComplyJet and Wolfia support?


ComplyJet imports Excel, Word, PDF, CSV and Google Sheets and exports back in the original format. Wolfia works on Excel, Word and PDF files and exports back in the original format, and its Chrome extension fills answers into web portals.
